result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random bipartite graph in which each cross pair is an edge with probability p. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random bipartite graph in which each cross pair is an edge with probability p. title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a random bipartite graph in which each cross pair is an edge with probability p. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a random bipartite graph in which each cross pair is an edge with probability `p`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14142-L14251){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_bipartite_gnp_graph( n1, n2, p, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, part_attr="part", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bipartite G(n1, n2, p) random graph](../assets/graphs/add-bipartite-gnp-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random bipartite graphs with three accent top nodes and four teal bottom nodes, where each of the 12 top-bottom pairs is joined independently with probability p=0.2, 0.5, and 0.8. Edges only ever run between the rows, and their number grows with p, from 2 to 4 to 8." width="100%"} Creates `n1` nodes in a first part and `n2` in a second, and joins each of the `n1 * n2` pairs across the parts independently with probability `p`. No edge runs inside a part, and the number of edges is random with mean `p * n1 * n2`. Pairs are skipped over in geometrically distributed jumps, so a sparse graph costs time in proportion to its edges rather than to `n1 * n2`. This is the bipartite version of `add_gnp_graph()` and NetworkX's `bipartite.random_graph()`. In a directed graph, every pair gets two independent chances, one for an edge from the first part to the second and one for an edge back, as with NetworkX's `directed=True`, so the expected edge count doubles. Each node's part is stored in the `part_attr=` node attribute (`0` for the first, `1` for the second), and the first part is created first. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random bipartite graphs are useful for: - null models for two-mode networks at a given density - test inputs for matching, projection and bipartite centrality algorithms - studying thresholds, such as when a perfect matching appears ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the first part. Must be non-negative. [n2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the second part. Must be non-negative. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability, between `0` and `1`, that a given cross pair is joined. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. [part_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["part"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's part (`0` or `1`). Default is `"part"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n1=` or `n2=` is negative or `p=` is outside `0` to `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Twenty by thirty nodes at `p=0.1` give about `0.1 * 20 * 30 = 60` edges: ::: {#5060901c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_bipartite_gnp_graph(20, 30, p=0.1, seed=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (50, 64) ``` ::: ::: No edge joins two nodes of the same part: ::: {#bd4b7aa8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.is_bipartite() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph each pair is tried in both directions: ::: {#7858e00c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph(directed=True).add_bipartite_gnp_graph(20, 30, p=0.1, seed=3).count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 140 ``` ::: :::
